standard.title: Spell with common letter patterns
standard.description: spell one- and two-syllable words with common letter patterns
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can understand that letters represent multiple sounds and that syllables contain vowel sounds (AC9E1LY12). They have not yet applied this knowledge to spell a range of one- and two-syllable words using common letter patterns systematically.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students spell one- and two-syllable words with common letter patterns.

nodes.label: Spelling one-syllable words with known patterns
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can spell one-syllable words using known letter patterns — including short vowels, consonant blends and digraphs.
nodes.minimum_width: Correctly spell at least five one-syllable words containing known letter patterns (e.g. short vowel, blend).
nodes.typical_width: Spell a range of one-syllable words using known letter patterns — CVC, CVCC, CCVC, digraphs — applying phoneme-grapheme knowledge to spell previously unwritten words.
wider: Generate and spell multiple words from the same pattern family (e.g. words ending in -st, -nd, -ng)
Apply spelling knowledge to write one-syllable topic vocabulary in content area writing
nodes.hinge_reason: Reliable one-syllable spelling is the foundation for the two-syllable strategy in N2 — students who cannot spell single syllables accurately cannot apply the 'spell each part' strategy to longer words.

response_modes.reason: Spelling requires more precision than reading — students can recognise correctly spelled words they cannot yet produce. Consolidation through varied writing contexts builds reliable spelling production.

success_criteria: Student correctly spells at least five one-syllable words with known patterns
Student can apply known patterns to spell a new, unfamiliar one-syllable word

nodes.label: Spelling two-syllable words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can spell one- and two-syllable words by applying syllable knowledge and known letter patterns.
nodes.minimum_width: Correctly spell at least three two-syllable words containing known blends or patterns.
nodes.typical_width: Spell two-syllable words by attending to each syllable separately, applying known letter patterns to each part — including words with common blends in either syllable.
wider: Explore two-syllable compound words and discuss how spelling each part separately helps
Write sentences using two-syllable topic vocabulary correctly spelled

response_modes.reason: Spelling two-syllable words requires a deliberate strategy: break the word into syllables, spell each part, then reassemble. A simple scaffold ('say it in parts, spell each part') makes this strategy explicit.

success_criteria: Student correctly spells at least three two-syllable words
Student can describe the strategy they use to approach spelling a two-syllable word
